ridings.name: Surrey South
ridings.communities: Panorama Ridge, Crescent, Grandview Heights, Hazelmere, Douglas (southern Surrey, inside the City of Surrey; does not include White Rock)

result_2024.note: Chapman won as a Conservative over NDP's Haroon Ghaffar. Only two candidates per Elections BC data.

ridings.mla_changes_since_2024: MLA Brent Chapman (elected as Conservative) joined OneBC on Sept 22, 2026, the day the writ dropped, after his wife Kerry-Lynne Findlay resigned as Conservative leader. OneBC then said he would not run; his name is not on the final Elections BC list. No sitting MLA is on the ballot here. Elenore Sturko (CentreBC leader), who won the 2022 Surrey South by-election, is running here but was the MLA for Surrey-Cloverdale at dissolution.

candidates.name: Parik Tahlan
candidates.bio: Security professional who works protecting high-profile people and organizations; longtime supporter of the Canadian Cancer Society.

candidates.name: Megan Knight
candidates.bio: White Rock mayor elected 2022 and city councillor 2014 to 2018; commissioned BC notary public since 1998; on the Metro Vancouver board and TransLink Mayors' Council as mayor.

sources.label: Daily Hive: Megan Knight to run in Surrey South

candidates.name: Elenore Sturko
candidates.bio: CentreBC leader since Sept 22, 2026; former RCMP staff sergeant and Surrey RCMP spokesperson; MLA for Surrey South (2022 by-election) then Surrey-Cloverdale (2024).

candidates.name: Bill McConnell
candidates.bio: Retired electrician who taught electrical apprentices at BCIT for 19 years; Red Seal certified; graduated from Delta Secondary School in Ladner.

candidates.name: Denis R Hurtubise
candidates.bio: Unaffiliated candidate. No published biography found in the sources checked.

ridings.notes: Elections BC web list shows Hurtubise as Unaffiliated (CSV says Other). In the CSV, Hurtubise and Surrey-Guildford's James Yaroshuk list the same financial agent address (262-5525 West Boulevard, Vancouver) as several OneBC candidates; no party link is stated anywhere, so both are recorded as independent. Wikipedia's candidate table shows Brent Chapman as incumbent with a not-seeking-re-election marker, consistent with the Elections BC list.

ridings.name: Surrey-Cloverdale
ridings.communities: Clayton and the Cloverdale town centre (southeast Surrey; Highway 15 on the west, Township of Langley on the east, 88 Avenue on the north)

result_2024.note: Wikipedia shows NDP at 9,681 (margin 587); Elections BC figure is 9,682 (margin 586).

ridings.mla_changes_since_2024: Elenore Sturko (elected as Conservative) was removed from the Conservative caucus on Sept 22, 2025 and sat as an independent, then joined CentreBC on Sept 18, 2026 and became its leader on Sept 22, 2026. Wikipedia lists her as CentreBC at dissolution; BC Election Guide lists her as Independent. She is running in Surrey South, not here. No sitting MLA is on the Cloverdale ballot.

ridings.name: Surrey-Serpentine River
ridings.communities: Area around the Serpentine River in south-central Surrey (riding formed from parts of the former Cloverdale, Panorama and Fleetwood ridings)

result_2024.note: Conservative gain; Hepner is a former Surrey mayor (2014 to 2018). Independent was Jim McMurtry.

ridings.mla_changes_since_2024: MLA Linda Hepner (Conservative) quit the Conservative caucus on Sept 20, 2026 over the removal of three MLAs and leadership, then rejoined about Sept 21 after Lorne Doerkson became interim leader. She is not running in 2026 and said she could not commit to another four years. No sitting MLA is on the ballot.

ridings.name: Surrey-White Rock
ridings.communities: City of White Rock and South Surrey (Semiahmoo peninsula), including the Semiahmoo First Nation reserve; Semiahmoo Bay on the south and west, Highway 99 on the east, 24 Avenue on the north

result_2024.note: Conservative gain from BC United (Halford was the incumbent). Wikipedia shows NDP at 12,699; Elections BC figure is 12,698.

ridings.mla_changes_since_2024: Trevor Halford (Conservative) was removed from the Conservative caucus on Sept 18, 2026 by then-leader Kerry-Lynne Findlay, and readmitted on Sept 21, 2026 by interim leader Lorne Doerkson. He is running again as a Conservative. Surrey Now-Leader also described him as the party's former interim leader (as of Dec 2025).
